title: Tokenification load orchestrator: mixed-length TPS microbench
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build and maintain a focused microbenchmark harness that measures tokens-per-second across mixed sequence-length workloads (short, medium, long), tracks p95 latency regressions, and automatically surfaces regression candidates to the CI pipeline. This ticket covers spec, implementation, CI integration, baseline capture, and initial rollout for core model families used in hosted and dedicated deployments.
technical_design: Design goals: (1) realistic workload profiles derived from sampled production traces (anonymized), (2) configurable mix ratios for seq-length bins, (3) warm/cold KV cache modes, (4) per-model variant measurement (fp16, int8, 4-bit), (5) automated baseline comparison using historical windows, and (6) lightweight alerting when p95 drift exceeds configurable thresholds. Implementation components: a Go-based runner that exercises the runtime via the local gRPC test harness, workload generator that replays tokenized sequences with controlled inter-request spacing, collector that aggregates tokens/sec and latency histograms, and a regression detector that pushes findings to the CI annotations API. Benchmarks will run in two modes: smoke (fast checks on PR) and full (daily/weekly scheduled runs on dedicated infra). Metrics are exported to Prometheus + S3 snapshots for diffs. We will reuse the existing token velocity harness where sensible but replace its steady-state assumptions with sequence-mix scenarios and KV warmup toggles.
acceptance_criteria:
- Harness can generate at least three configurable profiles: short-heavy (70% <64 tokens), balanced (33/33/33 short/medium/long), and long-heavy (50% >1024 tokens).
- Captures tokens/sec, p50, p95, p99, and sample latency histograms for each model/variant.
- Supports explicit KV cache modes: cold, partial-warm, fully-warm.
- CI smoke job runs in <15m and fails PRs if tokens/sec drops by >8% or p95 increases by >25% compared to the latest stable baseline.
- Full job publishes snapshot JSON to s3://redwood-benchmarks/tps-snapshots/<date>/<model>-<variant>.json and records Prometheus metrics.
- Regression detector opens a ticket template with prefilled artifacts (diff link, top N latency regressors) when threshold breached.
- Docs: README with runbook, config knobs, and how to add a new model to the suite.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for workload generator and collector logic. 2) End-to-end smoke against a local dev runtime with a small toy model. 3) Canary run against a dedicated test GPU pool (1x A10) to validate tokens/sec numbers and KV cache toggles. 4) Nightly full profile run against core models (rwl-1, rwl-2, open-compat-XL) with snapshot comparison. 5) Introduce synthetic regression (add artificial latency) to validate the detector and CI annotation flow. 6) Performance sensitivity matrix: sequence length vs batch size vs kv-warm state.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Merge harness into bench repo, enable PR smoke job (opt-in for first week). Phase 2: Enable smoke job by default and run nightly full profile against non-production test pool. Phase 3: After two weeks of stable baselines, enable automated ticket creation for regressions. Phase 4: Integrate with Console alerting and attach per-model dashboards to runtime-1.20 release notes.
